items.title: Kentavious Caldwell-Pope negotiating buy out from Grizzlies, to sign with 76ers
items.summary: Kentavious Caldwell-Pope won his first ring next to LeBron James, now he is headed to Philadelphia to try and do it again.Caldwell-Pope and the Grizzlies are working out a buyout, and once the veteran wing clears waivers, he intends to sign with the Philadelphia 76ers, reports NBA insider Chris Haynes.KCP moving on from Memphis is not a surprise. He was brought in while the team still had Ja Morant and Jaren Jackson Jr. and was looking to win. With the Grizzlies pivoting to a youth movement — plus they are dealing with a roster crunch — it makes sense to buy out KCP, who is set to make $ 21.6 million this season. items.summary: LeBron James was named the NBA Finals' Most Valuable Player all four times his team won the NBA title [Getty Images]LeBron James has announced he will be joining the Philadelphia 76ers next season for what he says will be his final contract in the NBA.The 41-year-old, the highest points scorer in the history of the league, left the Los Angeles Lakers after eight years last month. items.title: LeBron James, the 76ers and the legacy in the balance
items.summary: So, it's the Philadelphia 76ers for LeBron James. Weird choice, right?Of all the teams, of all the places, Philadelphia? It felt like it was going to be someplace more significant, somewhere more meaningful, but it's the Sixers.I guess they give him the best chance to win a championship, because that starting lineup — James, Tyrese Maxey, VJ Edgecombe, Jaylen Brown and Joel Embiid — it's a bear. It's an awfully big bet on the health of Embiid, who is rarely healthy these days, but it's a bet on a championship, and that is what it's all about for LeBron at this point.After all, he's always been in pursuit of Michael Jordan's six rings."My motivation," James once told a Nike skills academy camper, according to a 2016 Sports Illustrated profile, "is this ghost I'm chasing. The ghost played in Chicago."James currently ranks fourth on our Bill Russell Scale of greatest careers in NBA…
